briefFidelity: This is the finding, and it is not marginal. Blind, before reading a word of the brief, I described soft overlapping circles forming a fog-blob with a cluster of randomly rotated pale sticks like pick-up-sticks or jackstraws, and scattered debris squares in the margins. The brief asks for ARCADE: repeated bays seen head on, a colonnade abstracted until only interval and weight remain, the same member at a different scale nested inward toward the centre, engineered rather than drawn, regular, load-bearing, slightly severe. Almost every load-bearing noun in that brief is absent. There is no repetition anywhere in the twelve: 9190, 9906, 10443 and 10980 are splayed asterisks of sticks at arbitrary angles, and 9548, 9727, 10085 and 10264 are dense unstructured scribbles. There is no interval, because there is no rhythm to space out. There is no member repeated at descending scale marching inward: the stacked ellipses in 9011 and 9369 are the closest gesture, and they read as two or three overlapping soft blobs offset vertically into a peanut, not as nested bays. Nothing is head on or flattened into structure, because the soft radial gradient-free circles are the only geometry and they read as body, not as architecture. Nothing is engineered; every element is soft-edged, blurred at the overlaps, and rotated off-axis. And the one specified colour event, the single warm accent marking the innermost bay, does not exist in any of the twelve seeds or any of the three states. I wrote before reading the brief that there is essentially no chroma in the work at all. A reader shown these tiles and asked what they are would not say colonnade, arcade, bay, column or structure. The gate fails.
composition: There is a focal centre but it is arrived at by default rather than by design. In all twelve seeds the slate blob is planted dead centre, occupying most of the frame height and about half its width, with two symmetrical columns of empty black at left and right that nothing uses except the stray squares in 9727, 9906 and 10980. The bar cluster is the only incident with any contrast, so it takes the eye, but it sits as a small pale smudge inside a much larger soft mass that has no internal structure to relate it to. Frame use is weak: the work floats in the middle of the tile in neutral and recovery, and in stress it solves that only by overflowing and clipping at three edges, which is not the same as using the frame. In 9190 and 10264 the bars run out past the blob into black with no acknowledgement, so the blob reads as a backdrop the sticks are not actually inside rather than as a body containing them. Hierarchy exists, but it is one small pale mark against one large flat field, repeated twelve times.
collectionCoherence: This axis is the work's real strength and I want to credit it plainly. Laid out together, eleven of the twelve unmistakably belong to one project: the same slate blue-grey blob at the same centred position, the same pale warm-grey translucent bars, the same near-black ground, the same very narrow value range. Nothing in 9011, 9369, 9548, 9727, 9906, 10085, 10264, 10443, 10801 or 10980 looks like it wandered in from another run. The exception is 10622, which does not read as a member of the set: its blob is displaced down and left, its bars have become wide horizontal planks stacked like slats rather than crossing sticks, and a band of dark grey squares and pentagons runs across the top and down the left edge, clipped mid-shape by the frame. On a contact sheet 10622 reads as a different generator. One outlier in twelve is a coherence problem worth naming, though it is not what decides this review.
palette: Chosen and consistent, and genuinely restrained in the way the brief wants, but incomplete against what was specified and short of contrast in practice. Iron and ash over near-black is a fair description of what is here: one cool slate blue-grey for the mass, one pale warm grey for the bars, mid-grey for the marginal squares, near-black ground. The ground supports rather than competes, and the cool-versus-warm grey relation is the only chromatic idea in the work and it is a decent one. But the contrast range is doing very little: the bars sit only a few steps above the blob, so in 9011, 10801 and 9369 the cluster is a faint smudge rather than a mark, and where bars overlap the brightening is the sole tonal event in the frame. Critically, the brief names one warm accent marking the innermost bay, and there is no accent of any kind in any seed or state. The bars are marginally warm as a whole class, which is not an accent, and there is no innermost bay for one to mark.
seedVariation: The variation is real but confined to a minority of the pixels, and it fails in the narrow direction rather than the wide one. The dominant element by far, the slate blob, is effectively constant across all twelve in position, scale, silhouette and tone, so the differences live entirely inside the small central bar cluster. Within that cluster the range is genuine at 256px: 9369 and 10801 hold a tight little knot, 9011 a small tilted stack, 10443 a thin sparse jack of long sticks, 9548 and 10085 a dense radiating mass, 9190 and 9980 wide splayed diagonals. But these are not twelve different works; they are one work with its central scribble reshuffled, and the reshuffling is arbitrary rotation rather than a family of related configurations. In the opposite direction 10622 overshoots and stops looking like the same project at all. So the set is simultaneously too narrow across eleven and too wide at one.
thumbnailSurvival: Looking only at the 120px sheets, the twelve resolve into roughly four recognisable kinds rather than twelve things. The silhouette survives and the pale cluster survives as a smudge, but the individual bars merge and their angles are gone, which removes the one axis on which the seeds actually differ. What repeats twelve times is the same grey lozenge on black with a pale mark in the middle of it. The kinds I can separate are: tiny knot (9369, 10801, 9011), dense pale scribble mass (9548, 9727, 10085, 10264), long crossing sticks (9190, 9906, 10443, 10980), and 10622. Within those groups I cannot tell 9548 from 10085, or 9190 from 9906, at browse size. Tellingly, the most reliable discriminator at 120px is the scatter of small marginal squares, clearest in 9727 with its column of four squares left and three diamonds right, which means the least considered element in the frame is carrying the identity load. Low contrast makes this worse: pale grey on mid blue-grey loses more at 120 than a harder-edged drawing would.
marketResponse: The states are visibly different, but the change is not the change that was claimed, and that distinction is the whole axis. What I recorded blind is that the transition is almost entirely SCALE: in stress the blob inflates and pushes past the tile on the left, right and bottom, cropping its own silhouette away and turning the tile into a large flat grey field, while the bar cluster stays about the same absolute size and so reads proportionally smaller. The brief says that under drawdown the structure should lose members and the interval widen, as though bays were being removed from the run. Nothing is removed in 9011, 9190, 9369 or 9548 stress; the frame gets fuller and heavier, not sparser, and the only elements that actually disappear are the marginal squares, which are pushed out of frame by the enlargement rather than deleted from a run. The claimed direction is inverted. Recovery is meant to fill the colonnade back in and deepen the nesting; instead recovery returns to approximately neutral, and at 120px 9011, 9190 and 9369 recovery are hard to tell from their own neutral tiles at all. Only 9548 shows a genuine reconfiguration in recovery, a re-rotated cluster with a new long diagonal at bottom-left.
tokenIdentity: This axis passes cleanly and is the second thing the work does well. Same seed across neutral, stress and recovery is unmistakably the same token in all four seeds shown. 9011 keeps its small tilted left-leaning stack, 9190 its wide crossing diagonals, 9369 its tiny central knot, and 9548 its dense radiating mass, and in every case the silhouette, the cluster position, the cluster character and the palette persist through the transition. Nothing is replaced by another object under drawdown. If anything the identity is held too tightly: 9369 neutral and 9369 recovery are so close at 120px that they read as the same image, which is a marketResponse failure caused by the same conservatism that makes this axis succeed.
artifacts: Several, and one of them is systemic. The stress row clips the blob hard at the left, right and bottom edges in all four of 9011, 9190, 9369 and 9548, and it reads as scale overflow rather than as a compositional decision, because the crop lands arbitrarily on a soft round edge with no element aligned to the frame. 10622 clips its band of dark squares and pentagons mid-shape at the left edge, and repeats the clipped band again at bottom-left, which reads as a mistake rather than a bleed. Marginal squares sit half off the frame in 9906 and 10980. In 9190, 9906 and 10264 bars extend past the blob into open black and simply stop, with no edge or shadow acknowledging the boundary they crossed. The translucent overlaps in the dense seeds, 9548 and 10085 particularly, mush together into an undifferentiated pale mass at 120px where individual members can no longer be counted.
reasoning: I refuse this on briefFidelity, and the strength of the finding is that it was fixed before I read the brief. My blind description names soft overlapping circles, a fog or stone body, and randomly rotated sticks like pick-up-sticks, with no chroma and no repetition anywhere in the frame. The brief commissions an arcade: repeated bays, a colonnade flattened to interval and weight, the same member nested inward at descending scale, engineered and load-bearing and severe, with one warm accent at the innermost bay, losing members and widening its interval under drawdown. The output has no repetition, no interval, no nesting, no head-on structure, no accent, and its drawdown response inflates and crops the frame rather than thinning a run. That is the reviewer-prompt failure pattern exactly: the brief says one thing and the pictures read as another. The work is not incompetent, and I want that on the record, because refusing it is not a judgement on its craft. Eleven of twelve cohere, token identity holds perfectly across all three states, the iron-and-ash restraint is real, and the seeds do differ meaningfully at 256px. But this is a gate, and a competent organic softbody piece is not an answer to a brief about architecture. It also fails on its own separate terms at browse size, where twelve seeds collapse to four kinds and the state change reads as a zoom, so I am not refusing on the gate alone. One sentence decided it: the commissioned subject is the rhythm of repeated supports, and there is no repetition of any element anywhere in these twelve frames.
wouldChange: Build the bay as an actual repeated member and let repetition, not rotation, be the generator. Concretely: replace the stack of soft circles with a single hard-edged arch or post-and-lintel silhouette, then instance it four to seven times at a geometric scale ramp nested toward the frame centre on a shared axis, so the negative interval between members becomes the drawn subject and reads as rhythm at 120px. Kill the arbitrary rotation on the bars entirely; if members lean, let them lean by a repeating increment across the run, so the eye reads a rule rather than a scatter. Give members flat hard edges with no translucency at the overlaps, so the drawing is engineered rather than blurred, and widen the value gap between iron and ash so the structure survives thumbnail. Introduce the missing warm accent as a small saturated element occupying only the innermost bay, which also gives every tile a focal point and gives the nesting a destination. For market response, invert what stress currently does: hold the frame and the outermost bay fixed and DELETE members from the run, widening the interval between the survivors, so drawdown thins the colonnade visibly at 120px; let recovery re-add members and push the nesting one or two levels deeper rather than merely returning to the neutral scale. Never change global scale to signal state, since that crops the silhouette and inverts the claimed direction. Finally, resolve 10622, which is generating a different work, and drop or integrate the marginal squares, which currently carry identity by accident.
